original_test_intent: Validate the five FH chip-temperature channels numbered 11 through 15 against the approved FH thermal specification across complete IB/OOB SDR, Sensor List and BMC Web evidence.
original_method: The platform owner defines FH, explains the 11–15 numbering segment, binds each exact sensor to a physical FH chip and stable device identity, defines sensing source and operating envelope, and automation collects passively.
manual_activity: The FH/platform owner defines FH, the reason this case covers indices 11–15, maps the five chips and sensing points, approves operating-state limits and reviews the complete evidence separately from FH TRX sensors.
required_inputs: Authoritative FH definition and component role
Exact TEMP_FH11_Chip through TEMP_FH15_Chip naming syntax and fitted count
Explanation of the 11–15 segment and whether FH1–FH10 are covered elsewhere or absent
Board revision, physical coordinate and stable device/serial/fabric identity per chip
Sensing source: on-die junction, internal/remote diode or nearby board probe
Units, scale, tolerance, sample interval, freshness and unavailable semantics
Ranges/thresholds by traffic/workload, link, power, airflow and ambient state
SDR entity/name/description plus Sensor List/Web mapping, same-target revisions and independent recovery
safety_requirements: Resolve five exact names rather than treat `FH11~15_Chip` as one sensor
Do not infer FH meaning, fabricate FH1-FH10 coverage or reuse FH TRX readings
Bind each channel to a stable physical/device identity and sensing source
Capture operating state passively without creating traffic or workload
Do not alter links/drivers/cooling/thresholds/BMC or clear logs
Stop on numbering/population ambiguity, missing identity, stale/invalid value, device/link fault or thermal event
agent_execution_scope: Verify unique source, FH definition, numbering segment and five-name expansion
Verify FH chip topology and same-target stable identities read-only
Collect complete IB/OOB SDR and Sensor List, five exact chip results and BMC Web
Compare identity/value/state/freshness with passive traffic/link/power/airflow/SEL context
Perform no TRX substitution, workload/traffic, link/driver action, mutation, retry or verdict
engineer_actions: Define FH and approve FH11-FH15 physical/stable-device map
Explain the numbering segment and excluded FH indices
Define chip sensing source and state-specific limits distinct from TRX
Review all five chip channels and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

modernized_recommendation.status: REQUIRES FH11-FH15 SEGMENT DEFINITION, FIVE-CHIP MAP AND SENSOR SEMANTICS
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a five-row map from exact FH11–FH15 sensor string to board/device identity, coordinate, sensing source and approved operating envelope, with a documented boundary for FH1–FH10.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the unusual starting index and `_Chip` suffix expansion explicit, preventing silent assumptions about omitted FH indices or component type.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: The next TRX case and any earlier FH1–FH10 cases remain separate coverage and cannot be inferred from these five readings.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A partial-number segment can reflect a different board zone or component generation; applying limits or topology from lower indices without owner mapping can misclassify a localized thermal problem.

project_override_considerations: If FH11–FH15 are aliases, spares or unpopulated positions, the owner-approved inventory and uniqueness rule govern. No missing lower index may be counted or failed by inference.

Five physical/stable-device identities and sensing-source map
Units, scale, freshness and operating-state-qualified thermal criteria
Complete redacted IB/OOB SDR and Sensor List plus five exact results
